executive_summary: Recent CISA KEV and GitHub advisories reveal critical authentication bypass, path traversal, and DoS vulnerabilities in network devices, web frameworks, and libraries, urging immediate mitigation in labs and projects.

signals.title: @angular/router: Denial of Service via Unmatched Empty-Path Outlet Route Matching in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
signals.what_changed: Unmatched empty-path route matching creates infinite routing loops in SSR
signals.why_it_matters: Prevents DoS attacks by enforcing strict route validation
signals.application: Add route guard tests and limit empty-path handling in Angular SSR projects

signals.title: Hono: `serveStatic` decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths
signals.what_changed: Second decoding of request path bypasses static file middleware
signals.why_it_matters: Highlights need for proper path normalization to stop directory traversal
signals.application: Write middleware tests that verify path normalization and prevent double-decoding attacks

signals.title: @angular/platform-server: Open Redirect via Protocol-Relative URLs in Server-Side Rendering (SSR)
signals.what_changed: Protocol-relative URLs enable open redirect when SSR processes them
signals.why_it_matters: Open redirects can be abused for phishing and undermine trust
signals.application: Add URL validation and whitelist checks in Angular SSR applications

signals.title: Compress/s2: Integer Overflow or Wraparound and Out-of-bounds Write in compress
signals.what_changed: Integer overflow in compress leads to out-of-bounds write, enabling memory corruption
signals.why_it_matters: Shows risk of unchecked arithmetic in data processing libraries
signals.application: Perform static analysis and fuzz testing on compression libraries to detect overflow issues

signals.title: Fortinet Multiple Products contain a path traversal vulnerability that may allow an authenticated attacker with admin profile and at least read-write permissions to write or delete
signals.what_changed: Path traversal via CLI commands enables arbitrary file write/delete on FortiOS/FortiPAM
signals.why_it_matters: Critical for securing network device management interfaces and preventing data tampering
signals.application: Create lab environment with FortiOS VM and test CLI sanitization to block path traversal commands

experiment.title: Path Traversal via CLI Commands in a Simulated Network Device
experiment.objective: Demonstrate detection and mitigation of path traversal vulnerabilities in CLI-based administration interfaces.
prerequisites: Ability to run a vulnerable Python script
steps: Pull a minimal Ubuntu container using `docker run -it ubuntu:latest /bin/bash`.
Create a vulnerable script `vuln_cli.py` that executes `os.system('cat ' + user_path)` without sanitization.
Run the script with a legitimate path such as `/etc/passwd` to verify it works.
Attempt a path traversal payload like `../../../../etc/shadow` to confirm arbitrary file read.
Implement mitigation by normalizing the path with `os.path.realpath` and checking the resolved path stays within an allowed directory.
Re‑run the traversal payload to verify the mitigation blocks access.
expected_evidence: Script prints contents of `/etc/passwd` when given a valid path.
Traversal payload outputs `/etc/shadow` (or error) showing unauthorized access.
After mitigation, traversal payload returns 'access denied' and no file is read.
experiment.stop_condition: When mitigation is verified and the script no longer allows arbitrary file access via path traversal, within 60 minutes.

discarded: All other CISA KEV items older than 7 days and GitHub advisories beyond the selected five.
